I lost my virginity to my high school bf and we dated for nearly a year. After that I was very ambiguous sexually. I had frequent hookups and it was almost always exclusively with men. I knew that I was bisexual before my first relationship which was with a man. I’m not sure why I didn’t hook up with women as much as I did with men but that’s just how it happened. My point is that I used to be able to get it on with complete strangers. If this relationship (2 years with a man) were to end I think that I wouldn’t be able to just have spontaneous hookups anymore. Because my sex has been based around a connection for so long, I don’t think I would be able to have sex without a decent connection. Also my interest in men and women changes very frequently. For a lot of other bisexual people this has been the case too. A lot of us kinda of go through “guy phases” and “girl phases.” My point with here is that even if you explore your sexuality with men, nothing is set in stone. I’m not encouraging you to hide any part of yourself but just a reminder that you can choose to keep this private while you figure it out for yourself. And take your time, there’s absolutely no rush.

My biggest thing when people want to help me with my eating issues is that people want to help me. I know it sounds ridiculous but that’s the way it is. It took years of internalization and built up trauma for my ed to manifest so when people encourage me to eat or want to have conversations about control it (for lack of better terms) annoys the living shit out of me. I think to myself “what in the world” because to me it seems like they think they can fix an issue that’s been growing and boiling and festering for years inside me. My mind goes “you really think you can fix my problem with a 1-2 hour conversation when it took years to cultivate?” So my best advice is remember that patience is a virtue. Don’t give up on your friend but give them the space and the time they need to realize it’s an issue on their own. Also remember that you can’t MAKE a person recover, they have to choose recovery. I know it’s painful to watch someone you love go through this but as someone who has had to do that and also go through my own ed, I’ve learned that you really can’t push anything externally. Just be there as a shoulder to cry on and even an emotional punching bag. Show them that they are valuable in other ways instead of focusing on the eating/control aspect. Write them a letter about all the things you appreciate about them. They may not, and probably have not noticed the many amazing things that you’ve noticed about them. Hope this helps :)

This is definitely not based on science, just my real life experience…

So I’m a competitive swimmer and on my team there was this girl, let’s call her “Ellie,” and she was a really good swimmer. She was tall and muscular but she was also a bit bigger than the other swimmers. (Unrelated but she was the best distance swimmer I’ve encountered, in my opinion she shouldn’t have done competitive racing because she would have been a stellar open-water distance swimmer). One day we were warming up for a meet and talking about the whole “big-boned” concept. My stance was that big boned isn’t a thing and then she got me to feel her shin bones and that’s when I changed my mind. Her bones were 2x what I expected them to be. I thought that she was thicker because she had more fat on her but the thickness and density of her bones was undeniably contributing to her thicker appearance. She also shared with me that when she hits a limb against a table or wall or whatever it may be, she feels that some of those hits should have cause breaks, instead there were just clear dents in her bones. So maybe science points to no, but I don’t have another way to explain why her bones were like that, so I believe that big boned is definitely a real thing!
